CausalChain: Inflammatory stimuli -> Elevated IL-6 secretion -> IL-6 binds its receptor activating JAK2 -> Activated JAK2 phosphorylates STAT3 -> STAT3 translocates to the nucleus and upregulates DNMT1 expression -> Increased DNMT1 activity epigenetically silences tumor suppressor genes -> Enhanced cancer stem cell maintenance and chemoresistance
Hypothesis: Combining inhibitors of the IL-6/JAK2/STAT3 signaling axis with DNMT1 inhibitors will disrupt the epigenetic feed-forward loop that sustains cancer stemness and therapy resistance, thereby improving treatment efficacy in cancers characterized by chronic inflammation and epigenetic dysregulation.
Abstract: We propose that the interplay between inflammatory signaling via the IL‐6/JAK2/STAT3 axis and epigenetic regulation mediated by DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1) forms a critical feed‐forward loop that not only sustains cancer stem cell properties but also underlies chemoresistance in solid tumors. Our hypothesis is that simultaneous inhibition of IL‐6 signaling and DNMT1 activity may disrupt this loop, resulting in the restoration of tumor suppressor gene expression and enhanced sensitivity to conventional chemotherapeutics. This dual‐targeting strategy offers a novel therapeutic approach for cancers such as colorectal and pancreatic adenocarcinomas, where aberrant IL‐6/JAK2/STAT3 activation and epigenetic silencing are common.
